description: ETHOS.TSAM is a Python time-series aggregation package developed at Forschungszentrum Jülich's Institute of Climate and Energy Systems. It reduces model inputs by selecting typical periods, decreasing time resolution or combining both operations. Pandas input series can include weather and loads; outputs include representative periods, reconstructed series and accuracy measures. Coverage is global and input-dependent, with period duration and resolution chosen by the user. Public source and examples are free under MIT, with HiGHS installed by default and optional commercial solvers under separate terms. A limitation is the loss of temporal information during aggregation, particularly where storage or rare extremes matter. Version 4 removes the older TimeSeriesAggregation class, so existing workflows need migration. The package can reduce energy-system optimisation size and complements PyPSA (model-pypsa). A first-review FINE draft mentions TSAM as a dependency, but does not represent this independently maintained general input-processing package. The cited 2022 study describes temporal-aggregation methods. No aggregation or optimisation was run.
